_comment: Copy to ~/.claude/guard-config.json. Every key is OPTIONAL — without this file the guard runs on its defaults, in English. Point CLAUDE_GUARD_CONFIG elsewhere to use a different path (test setups only; the production hook ignores environment variables).
_comment_language: Message language. Omit it, or leave it out entirely, and every message is English — English is built into the hook and always available. Set a code and the hook looks for lang/<code>.json next to itself. Missing keys fall back to English, so a half-finished translation still works. Shipped: de.

installation._comment_installation: Where this machine keeps things. Every entry is optional; omitted ones use the default. Paths may start with ~.
installation._comment_rules: Where the rules file lives. Default: ~/.claude/safety-guard/security-rules.json. Set this when you keep your rules in a checkout you version-control. It does two things at once: the hook LOADS from here, and the path is added to self-protection — so pointing it somewhere else does not leave that file writable.
installation._comment_hook_source: Where the hook's own sources live. This does NOT change what runs — it adds the directory to self-protection, and dev mode opens exactly it. Set it when the installed hook is a symlink into a checkout, so the protection follows the real files instead of the link.
installation._comment_dev_window: Flag file for dev mode. Default: ~/.claude/.hook-dev-mode. Its presence and expiry decide whether the owner has opened the supervised window.
installation._comment_lang_dir: Where the language files live, if not next to the hook. Only needed when the hook is a single file somewhere the lang/ directory could not follow.
installation._comment_approval_scripts: Directory of the owner's approval scripts. Default: ~/.claude/bin. A configured directory is added to self-protection, like rules and hook_source -- the chain approval channel below runs a script from here.

_comment_chain_approval: Approving from a distance, without the ! channel. OFF unless enabled. When on, the assistant may run the approval script itself in exactly ONE form: '<approval_scripts>/<script> --code <one-time value> <id> <level flag> 1|2|3 <scope flag> /path [<minutes flag> N]'. Matched against the whole command line -- any prefix, chained command or other path falls back to the hard owner-only block. The one-time value comes from the owner and must be unpredictable for the assistant; the approval script checks it. Script name and flag names describe YOUR approval script's interface. The shipped grant-override does not take --code yet, so leave this off until your script does.
_comment_update_check: Check once a day whether a newer guard is published, and say so at session start. OFF by default and it is the ONLY part of this tool that contacts anything: a security tool that phones home uninvited spends the trust it needs, so this is your decision, not the default. Turn it on and one plain-text request per interval goes to the source below; the answer must look like a date or it is ignored, and nothing fetched is ever executed. It only REPORTS — installing an update stays a separate, deliberate step. Any failure (no network, bad answer, unreadable file) ends in silence rather than a daily complaint.

update_check._comment_enabled: true turns the daily check on. Left out or false, nothing leaves this machine.
update_check._comment_interval_hours: Hours between two real checks. Default 24. Session starts in between only read a timestamp.
update_check._comment_source: Where the published version is read from. Must be https — an unencrypted answer could be tampered with in transit, and this one decides what you get told about security. Point it at your own fork if you track one.
